Great to speak today. Quick recap from our discovery and the immediate asks so we can align on the Dedicated capacity pilot: 

- Goals: support LumenHealths triage assistant with predictable sub-150ms median token latency for completion requests and scale to ~200 QPS peak for short-form clinical summaries (avg prompt+completion ~512 tokens).
- Traffic shape: expected steady baseline ~25 QPS, daily peaks up to ~200 QPS for 10-15 minute windows during shift changes; concurrency per request path likely 40-80 concurrent generation calls depending on batching.
- Embeddings/rerankers: well use embeddings for semantic search (batching offline + on-demand embedding calls) and a lightweight reranker for top-k scoring (model small CPU-bound).

Immediate asks for our sizing worksheet (attached):
1) Confirm expected peak QPS, percent synchronous vs async, and SLA window for tail latency (p50/p95/p99).
2) Confirm whether LumenHealth traffic will originate from private VPC (preferred) or public egress. If VPC, share CIDR and peering timeline.
3) Any constraints on caching of PII or request logging?

Ive attached a draft sizing sheet and our autoscale playbook. Aditya (copied) will follow up with implementation notes (SDK/auth, routing, tool-calling patterns, and queue sizing math).

Suggested next steps:
- You review the sizing sheet and return with the fields above by EOD Wed (11/4).
- Aditya will propose a pilot topology and can run a quick PoC with sample traffic the week of 11/9 if procurement is OK.

- Sync vs async: ~80% synchronous (user-facing completions), ~20% async (batch reranks/embeddings).
- Latency targets: p50 <120ms, p95 <300ms, p99 <700ms for the user-facing path.
- Average payload: prompts avg ~120 tokens inbound, completion ~390 tokens outbound (total ~510 tokens).
- Embeddings: ~10k requests/day typical, with bursts during dataset reindexing. Reranker is small and we can run it on CPU nodes.

Hi John / team 

Thanks for the details  helpful. I pulled together a short implementation checklist below and a sizing/queueing recommendation based on the 200 QPS peak and ~510-token average. See attached playbook and sizing sheet for the worksheet Ill use during the PoC.

1) SDK / auth / setup
- SDK: we recommend using Redwood official SDK (node/python) with streaming enabled for user-facing completions. Example: client.generate({model: "redwood-dedicated-1", stream: true, max_tokens: 512}).
- Auth: API keys for the private deployment; for VPC peering we use mutual TLS + short-lived service tokens. Well coordinate KMS integration for keys at rest.
- Routing: policy-based routing by route tag. You can route high-priority traffic (UI completions) to low-latency pool; background batches to a cheaper reserve pool.

2) Structured output / tool calling / rerankers
- Structured output: use function/tool calling for deterministic structured responses (JSON schema). Recommend validating at the proxy layer and falling back to free-text on failures.
- Reranker: run as a lightweight scoring service (CPU). Use embeddings for recall + rerank scored by small model. Keep reranker calls asynchronous when possible to avoid blocking UI flows.

3) Autoscaling, queue sizing, concurrency math (recommendation)
- Assumptions: avg tokens per request = 510, avg token generation latency per GPU = 1.8ms/token (optimized quantized runtime), effective batching gives 1.6x throughput improvement under steady state.
- Per-request mean processing time estimate: 510 tokens * 1.8ms = ~918ms raw; with batching improvement expect ~575ms effective per request at 1x concurrency.
- Concurrency sizing: to support 200 QPS steady peak with target p95 <300ms we need to rely on batching + sufficient GPU slots. Practical approach: target 250 concurrent generator slots (to absorb bursts and variability) across the pool, with autoscale floor sized for baseline (25 QPS => ~40 slots) and max scale to 300 slots.
- Queueing: maintain a short in-memory request queue per worker and a per-tenant global queue. Recommended queue depth: 500 requests with weighted routing (UI requests prioritized). Use adaptive rejection: beyond 500 requests, degrade to async (enqueue) with a 202 response and resume processing when capacity returns. This keeps client SLA predictable.
- Backpressure/circuit breaker behavior: Redwood supports graceful degradation policies:
  * Priority queuing and preemption of background jobs
  * Early 202/429 responses with Retry-After for non-critical requests
  * Canary fallback to smaller model variants for tail mitigation

4) PoC topology suggestion
- Pilot with a dedicated pool of 4 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) configured with:
  * autoscale min: 1 node (baseline), max: 6 nodes
  * target concurrency per GPU: 40-50 generator slots (tunable)
  * prefix/KV cache enabled for session reuse
- Observability: instrument per-route p50/p95/p99, token-level cost, and queue lengths. Well surface these in Redwood Console and wire alerts for sustained queue >300.

Next steps I propose:
- John/Sara: confirm VPC peering timeline and PO cadence (Sara)
- John: send finalized numbers in the sizing sheet by EOD Wed (11/4)  Ill iterate and produce a PoC runbook by 11/6.
- Marissa/Aditya: schedule a 30-min PoC kickoff the week of 11/9 to run sample traffic and validate queues/autoscale.
